lede: A tyrant killing the sons of a people; a mother told to put her baby in the river; a fugitive who helps two women at a well and is given a home. The life of Mūsā told in full, to a Prophet ﷺ about to become a fugitive himself — with a promise in the last lines that he would come back.

names.name: al-Qaṣaṣ
names.note: From its twenty-fifth ayah: when Mūsā came to the old man of Madyan “and told him the story”. It is also called Sūrat Mūsā, and Ṭā Sīn Mīm.

revelation.verdict: Makkan — with one ayah from the road of the Hijrah
revelation.detail: It is Makkan; al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrimah held all of it so. Ibn ʿAbbās excepted one ayah, the eighty-fifth, which came down at al-Juḥfah, on the road, as the Prophet ﷺ was leaving for Madinah — so that, as Ibn al-Jawzī puts it, it is neither Makkan nor Madinan. Muqātil also held four ayat about believers from the People of the Book (28:52–55) to be Madinan. The traditional order places the surah forty-ninth.
revelation.when: The last years in Makkah; one ayah on the road of the Hijrah itself

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها غَيْرَ آَيَةٍ مِنها، وهي قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ القُرْآنَ﴾ [القَصَصِ: ٨٥] فَإنَّها نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وهو بِالجُحْفَةِ في وقْتِ خُرُوجِهِ لِلْهِجْرَةِ، هَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ
مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَقَتَادَةُ إِلَّا آيَةً نَزَلَتْ بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ وَالْمَدِينَةِ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُوَيْهِ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في ”الدَّلائِلِ“، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ”القَصَصِ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: The believers in Makkah were few, poor and hunted, and the men who hunted them owned the city. This surah opens by telling them how Allah regards that arrangement: “Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing a group of them… And We wished to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders, and to make them the inheritors.”

It then tells the life of Mūsā from before he could speak. His mother is inspired to nurse him and, when she fears for him, to cast him into the river. Pharaoh’s own household takes him in. His sister follows at a distance; he refuses every nurse until he is returned to his mother. Grown, he strikes a man and kills him, and has to flee. At the water of Madyan he finds two women holding back their flock, waters it for them, and then sits in the shade and says: “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.” He is given work, a wife, and ten years. On the way back, with his family, he sees a fire.

Every stage is one the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions could recognise: the powerlessness, the flight, the years abroad, the return with a mission. And as he left Makkah by night, grieving at the sight of it, the ayah came down at al-Juḥfah: “He who ordained the Qurʾan for you will surely bring you back to a place of return.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: to Makkah.

The surah has a second tyrant, of a different kind. Qārūn was of Mūsā’s own people, and his treasure was such that its keys alone weighed down a band of strong men. “I was given it only because of knowledge I have,” he said. He went out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted this life said, “If only we had the like of what Qārūn has been given.” Then the earth swallowed him and his house. Quraysh, too, had their rich men — and one sentence from them is quoted: “If we follow the guidance with you, we shall be snatched from our land.”

occasions.title: Abū Ṭālib
occasions.text: When Abū Ṭālib was dying, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found Abū Jahl and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayyah with him. He said: “Uncle, say ‘lā ilāha illā Allāh’ — a word by which I can plead for you before Allah.” The two said: “Abū Ṭālib, will you turn from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?” They kept at him until the last thing he said was that he was upon the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. And Allah sent down about Abū Ṭālib: “You do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.”
occasions.source: Al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn: al-Bukhārī (4772) and Muslim (24).

occasions.title: At al-Juḥfah
occasions.text: On “He will surely bring you back to a place of return”, Ibn ʿAbbās said: “To Makkah.”

aim: To set out the true scales of power, by showing Allah’s might and His way of helping the oppressed and destroying the arrogant.

outline.title: The rule
outline.summary: Ṭā Sīn Mīm. We recite to you something of the news of Mūsā and Pharaoh, in truth. Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people factions, oppressing one group — slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. We wished to favour those who were oppressed in the land, and make them leaders and heirs.

outline.title: The infant in the river
outline.summary: We inspired the mother of Mūsā: nurse him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear or grieve; We shall return him to you. Pharaoh’s family picked him up, to be an enemy and a grief to them. Pharaoh’s wife said, “A comfort to my eye and yours; do not kill him.” We returned him to his mother, that her eye might be comforted.

outline.title: The flight, and Madyan
outline.summary: When he reached his full strength, We gave him judgement and knowledge. He struck a man and killed him: “My Lord, I have wronged myself; forgive me.” A man came running from the far side of the city: “Mūsā, the chiefs are conferring to kill you.” He left, afraid. At the water of Madyan he watered the flock of two women, then turned to the shade: “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.” One of them said, “Father, hire him: the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.”

outline.title: The call, and Pharaoh’s end
outline.summary: When Mūsā had completed the term and was travelling with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the Mount. He was called from the tree: “Mūsā, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.” Pharaoh said, “Chiefs, I know of no god for you other than me. Hāmān, kindle me a fire upon the clay and build me a tower, that I may look at the God of Mūsā.” We seized him and his hosts and flung them into the sea.

outline.title: You were not there — yet you tell it
outline.summary: You were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Mūsā, nor were you dwelling among the people of Madyan; but it is a mercy from your Lord. Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it: they will be given their reward twice over. You do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. They say: “If we follow the guidance with you, we shall be snatched from our land.” Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary?

outline.title: The Day He calls them
outline.summary: The Day He calls to them: “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?” Your Lord creates what He wills and chooses. If Allah made the night unending over you, what god but Allah could bring you light? From every nation We shall draw out a witness, and say: “Bring your proof.”

outline.title: Qārūn
outline.summary: Qārūn was of the people of Mūsā, and he oppressed them. We had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men. His people said: “Do not exult. Seek, through what Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world.” He said: “I was given it only for knowledge I possess.” He went out before his people in his adornment. Then We made the earth swallow him and his dwelling. That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who want neither exaltation in the land nor corruption.

outline.title: The return
outline.summary: He who ordained the Qurʾan upon you will surely bring you back to a place of return. You did not expect that the Book would be conveyed to you; it is only a mercy from your Lord. So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers. Call on no other god with Allah. Everything will perish but His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

keyAyah.why: Allah’s intention for the oppressed, stated before the story begins. Everything in the surah is its unfolding.

before: Al-Naml showed Mūsā at the fire, in a few ayat. Al-Qaṣaṣ tells how he came to be there, from the day he was born.
after: Al-Qaṣaṣ ends with the Prophet ﷺ promised a return after he is driven out. Al-ʿAnkabūt opens with those who are left: “Do people think they will be left to say, ‘We believe,’ and not be tested?”
